1753 is a common year starting on Monday (not a leap year).  
255 days before July 1, 1753:  
Step back 6 months (Jan–Jun): July 1 → Jan 1 is 182 days (Jan 31 + Feb 28 + Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 31 + Jun 30 = 181 days? Let's check: Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30 = 31+28+31+30+31+30 = 181 days from Jan 1 to Jul 1? Actually from Jan 1 to Jul 1 is 181 days, so Jul 1 back to Jan 1 is 181 days earlier.  
We need 255 days earlier: 255 − 181 = 74 days before Jan 1, 1753.  
Go into 1752: 1752 is a leap year (divisible by 4, Gregorian, 1752 in GB already using Gregorian).  
Dec 31, 1752 is 1 day before Jan 1, 1753.  
74 days before Jan 1 = Jan 1 minus 74 days = Oct 19, 1752 (since Oct 20 to Dec 31: Oct 20–31: 12 days, Nov 30, Dec 31: 30+31=61, total 73 days to Dec 31, so 74 days before Jan 1 = Oct 19).  

FINAL_ANSWER: 1752-10-19
